neighbours.caption: Atypical ductal hyperplasia. A Two adjacent ducts showing partial involvement by a proliferation of uniform cells forming cribriform structures. B The central portion of this duct contains an evenly placed population of uniform cells that forms a cribriform structure. Note the different cell population at the periphery, and the associated calcification.

Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of high nuclear grade. A Multiple spaces involved by DCIS of high nuclear grade, some with comedo necrosis and calcification. There is a chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate in surrounding stroma. B This space shows a rim of viable cells with high-grade nuclei. There is comedo-type necrosis and calcification. C Higher-power view of lesion shown in B. The cells show nuclear pleomorphism and several mitotic figures are evident. D Solid pattern with punctate necrosis. E Clinging pattern with significant nuclear pleomorphism and several mitotic figures. F DCIS of high nuclear grade involving lobular acini.

full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of pancreatic tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows an islet of Langerhans with prominent deposition of amorphous, eosinophilic material in and around the cells. This deposit replaces normal cellular architecture and is characteristic of amyloidosis. The most likely diagnosis is diabetes mellitus associated with islet amyloid deposition.

blind.description: This is a microscopic image of breast tissue showing multiple ducts involved by a neoplastic proliferation. The cells exhibit high-grade nuclei with marked pleomorphism, comedo-type necrosis, and associated calcifications. Surrounding the ducts, there is a chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate in the stroma. The most likely diagnosis is ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of high nuclear grade.

random.description: This is a photomicrograph of pancreatic tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows an islet of Langerhans with prominent amorphous eosinophilic deposits within the parenchyma. These hyaline deposits are characteristic of amyloidosis involving the pancreatic islets. This histological finding is frequently associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
